powershell -Command "Get-Process -Name 'Code' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -First 1"

But the tool might not capture exit code. It will capture stdout. So we can just run a command that prints status.

Let's produce a command that prints "VS Code is running" or "VS Code is not running".

We'll call the tool with command: powershell -Command "if (Get-Process -Name 'Code' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) { Write-Output 'VS Code is running' } else { Write-Output 'VS Code is not running' }"

Then we will get output. We'll then respond accordingly.
